summary.title: Pro Git (book, 2nd edition)
summary.one_liner: A free, openly licensed full book that takes you from Git basics through branching, servers, customization, and internals.
takeaways: The book is organized into ten chapters plus appendices covering basics, branching, servers, distributed workflows, and tools.
Chapter 3 covers branching and merging, including remote branches and rebasing.
Chapter 7 covers advanced tools such as interactive staging, rewriting history, reset, rerere, and submodules.
Chapter 10 explains Git internals: objects, references, packfiles, refspecs, and transfer protocols.
The content is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial Share Alike 3.0 and corrections are accepted via GitHub.
summary.summary: The Pro Git book, by Scott Chacon and Ben Straub (published by Apress), is read free online at git-scm.com. The page is a table of contents linking to chapters on getting started, basics, branching, Git on servers, distributed Git, GitHub, advanced tools, customizing Git, Git and other systems, and internals. Appendices cover Git in editors and shells, embedding Git libraries, and a command reference. The page notes that the content is Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 3.0 licensed and that the online version is updated by contributors via GitHub.
